chapters.title: Make islands of two
chapters.text: Choose one cat and one mouse. Everyone else lies side by side in pairs, with room to run between them.

chapters.title: The cat follows the mouse
chapters.text: The cat tries to make a gentle tag. The mouse can keep running or join an island.

chapters.title: Slow down and join one end
chapters.text: The mouse lies beside the left end of this pair. There are briefly three people.

chapters.title: The opposite person gets up
chapters.text: Player 2 leaves from the opposite end and becomes the mouse. The other two stay together.

chapters.title: A tag changes both roles
chapters.text: This time the cat reaches the mouse. Stop briefly to exchange roles.

chapters.title: Give the new mouse a head start
chapters.text: The tagged mouse is now the cat. The former cat gets three seconds to move away as the new mouse.

chapters.title: Pause and rotate the cat
chapters.text: After a minute, pause the chase. Choose a fresh cat, rebuild the pairs and start another timed round.

chapters.title: Agree where everyone may go
chapters.text: Set boundaries, a meeting point and a stop call. Choose a first hunter; this small example has three runners.

chapters.title: Hide, then begin the search
chapters.text: Runners get one minute to hide. Hunters search only within the agreed area; runners may keep moving.

chapters.title: A tag begins the change
chapters.text: The hunter gently tags runner 1. The caught runner announces it and counts to five before joining the search.

chapters.title: Caught runners become hunters
chapters.text: Runner 1 now searches too. The original hunter finds runner 2, who must also wait five seconds.

chapters.title: Hunt from more than one direction
chapters.text: The newest hunter joins. Hunter 1 catches the last free runner; there are no prisons or rescues in this version.

chapters.title: Stop when everyone is caught
chapters.text: All runners have changed sides, so the hunters win this round. If time expires first, the remaining runners win together.

chapters.title: Everyone returns to the meeting point
chapters.text: Count the whole group and rotate the first hunter. Give the runners a new hiding minute.

chapters.title: Pick a place everyone can fit
chapters.text: Choose one hider and accessible hiding areas. Everyone else waits at a meeting point.

chapters.title: Let the hider go first
chapters.text: Give the hider one minute. Then the others search independently or in pairs.

chapters.title: Finding means joining
chapters.text: Searcher 1 finds the hider. They quietly sit beside them instead of calling out the discovery.

chapters.title: Each finder makes the group bigger
chapters.text: Searcher 2 joins too. The last searcher must now find a whole hidden group.

chapters.title: The last searcher finds everyone
chapters.text: The shared reveal ends the round. Being last is a finale, not an elimination or penalty.

chapters.title: Return together and rotate
chapters.text: Regroup and choose a new hider. Use the agreed stop call if the search timer ends first.

chapters.title: Start with a linked pair
chapters.text: The two blob players link hands or elbows. Their free hands make gentle tags.

chapters.title: A catch joins the chain
chapters.text: Stop safely after the tag. Player 3 joins the blob, which now moves as a group of three.

chapters.title: Four people trigger a split
chapters.text: Another catch brings the blob to four. Four is the signal to divide.

chapters.title: Make two separate pairs
chapters.text: Break the middle link. Both pairs can now move and tag independently.

chapters.title: Each pair keeps growing
chapters.text: Both blobs catch another runner. Larger games repeat the grow-to-four, split-in-two rule until everyone joins.

chapters.title: Choose the next starting pair
chapters.text: This small round is complete. The last two caught can start together while everyone else spreads out.

chapters.title: Start behind one shore
chapters.text: All fish begin on the same shore. Only the octopus starts in the ocean.

chapters.title: Cross when the octopus calls
chapters.text: All fish travel to the other shore. The octopus moves to intercept fish before they reach safety.

chapters.title: A caught fish becomes a crab
chapters.text: Fish 1 was tagged. It stays at this exact spot for the rest of the round, with feet planted.

chapters.title: Cross back past the crabs
chapters.text: Fish 2 passes within the crab’s reach and becomes another crab. Fish 3 reaches the opposite shore safely.

chapters.title: The last fish is caught
chapters.text: On another crossing the octopus catches fish 3. All fish are now stationary, so the round ends.

chapters.title: Reset the ocean
chapters.text: Everyone becomes a fish again except the new octopus. Return the fish to one shore.

chapters.title: Find clear shadows
chapters.text: Choose a sunny open area and one tagger. The dark shapes are the players’ shadows on the ground.

chapters.title: Step on a shadow
chapters.text: The tagger steps on player 1’s shadow and calls their name and “caught”. No body contact is needed.

chapters.title: Give the new tagger room
chapters.text: Player 1 becomes the tagger. Pause briefly while the previous tagger moves away.

chapters.title: Find another moving shadow
chapters.text: The new tagger steps onto player 2’s shadow. Everyone plays honestly about the contact.

chapters.title: Keep everybody playing
chapters.text: Player 2 is now the tagger. The previous tagger returns to running after a brief pause.

chapters.title: Finish at the short timer
chapters.text: Call the stop. This is continuous play, with no elimination; swap the starting tagger for another round.

chapters.title: Choose connected court lines
chapters.text: Walk the allowed routes first. Everyone, including the tagger, must move along these lines.

chapters.title: A tagged runner blocks the line
chapters.text: The tagger reaches player 1. Player 1 stops exactly there and becomes a visible roadblock.

chapters.title: Use a different intersection
chapters.text: Player 2 takes the lower route. Runners cannot squeeze past roadblocks or jump a gap between lines.

chapters.title: Taggers can carefully walk around
chapters.text: The tagger walks around the roadblock, rejoins the clear line below it and follows it to catch player 2.

chapters.title: One runner ends this round
chapters.text: Player 3 is the last runner. Stop now, or stop at two minutes if more runners remain.

chapters.title: Everybody rejoins
chapters.text: Remove all roadblocks and choose a new tagger. Every chosen line is open again.

chapters.title: Everyone starts at zero
chapters.text: Set a three-minute timer. Every player may gently tag any other player.

chapters.title: Count one successful tag
chapters.text: Player 1 tags player 2 and adds one to their own count. Player 2 stays free to move.

chapters.title: Being tagged does not stop you
chapters.text: Player 2 immediately keeps playing and later tags player 3. Nobody freezes or sits out.

chapters.title: Find somebody different
chapters.text: Player 1 tags player 4 for a second point. Avoid immediate repeated tags on the same person.

chapters.title: Stop and compare your counts
chapters.text: Freeze at the stop signal. Compare counts or personal bests; all four players participated throughout.

chapters.title: Reset every score together
chapters.text: Everyone returns to zero. Start another short round with the same no-elimination rule.

chapters.title: Spread out and start the timer
chapters.text: Choose taggers and a two-minute round. The remaining players are free runners.

chapters.title: A tag makes you stationary
chapters.text: The tagger catches player 1. Player 1 stays still with hands held forward.

chapters.title: Bring two rescuers together
chapters.text: Two free runners approach the stuck player. Each touches one of the stuck player’s shoulders.

chapters.title: Clap the two free hands
chapters.text: While touching the shoulders, the rescuers clap their other hands together. That completes the rescue.

chapters.title: The rescued player can run
chapters.text: All three runners are free again. The tagger keeps chasing; a rescued player can be caught later.

chapters.title: End at the timer or full freeze
chapters.text: Here time runs out with free runners remaining, so the runners win. Taggers win if everyone becomes stuck first.

chapters.title: Choose new taggers
chapters.text: Reset every stuck player and rotate the tagger role before the next short round.

chapters.title: Face a partner at centre
chapters.text: Each pair starts between two home lines. Partners will run toward different homes.

chapters.title: Reveal rock, paper or scissors
chapters.text: Use the same count. Paper beats rock in these examples; replay any tied pair.

chapters.title: The winner becomes the chaser
chapters.text: A1 chases B1 toward the right home. In the other pair, B2 chases A2 toward the left home.

chapters.title: A tag or home ends the chase
chapters.text: B1 is tagged before home. A2 reaches home safely. Either result ends that pair’s chase.

chapters.title: Both partners return
chapters.text: Caught and safe players both come back to their original side. This version has no elimination or cumulative score.

chapters.title: Shift along for a new opponent
chapters.text: Move one line along to create new pairs. Play another reveal and chase, for five rounds in total.

chapters.title: Make one comfortable connected line
chapters.text: Use light hands on the hips or shoulders ahead, where comfortable. Front is head; back is tail.

chapters.title: Curl the dragon at walking pace
chapters.text: The head tries to gently tag the tail. Everyone moves together without pulling the line apart.

chapters.title: Stop if the connection breaks
chapters.text: This gap breaks the line. Everyone pauses immediately; the head cannot claim a tag during the break.

chapters.title: Reconnect and restart
chapters.text: Restore every connection before the chase continues. Keep a comfortable walking pace.

chapters.title: Tag the tail without breaking
chapters.text: The head reaches the tail while the dragon stays connected. Stop the whole line.

chapters.title: Move the head to the back
chapters.text: The old head becomes the new tail, and player 2 becomes head. Continue until everyone has led the dragon.

chapters.title: Give each team a flag and holding zone
chapters.text: You are safe on your own half. Agree space around flag and holding zones that defenders must respect.

chapters.title: Enter their half and take their flag
chapters.text: A1 crosses into slate territory and picks up the slate flag. It must come back across centre.

chapters.title: A tag sends the carrier to holding
chapters.text: B1 tags A1 before the return. The flag goes back to its zone, and A1 enters the slate holding area.

chapters.title: A free teammate can rescue one player
chapters.text: A2 reaches the holding zone and gently tags A1. That frees one held teammate.

chapters.title: The rescued pair walks safely home
chapters.text: Both players get a safe walk to their own half before rejoining. Meanwhile A3 makes a new attempt on the flag.

chapters.title: Cross centre with the flag to score
chapters.text: A3 carries the slate flag into the white half. That successful return scores one point.

chapters.title: Reset both flags and every player
chapters.text: Return the flags to their zones and release all held players. Keep the score; first to three returns wins.

chapters.title: Give captured opponents a rescue zone
chapters.text: Each team stays in its half. Caught players wait in the floor zone behind the opposing team.

chapters.title: Direct hits send players to waiting
chapters.text: These two below-waist hits send A2 and A3 to the rescue zone. Bounced hits do not count.

chapters.title: A waiting player can catch a pass
chapters.text: A1 recovers the ball and passes to waiting A2. The catch earns A2 a free walk home; an active-player catch has no extra bonus.

chapters.title: Shoot a basket from your half
chapters.text: A2 passes back and walks safely home. A1 scores in the opposing basket without crossing centre.

chapters.title: The whole waiting team comes back
chapters.text: Every white player still waiting may return. Pause throws for the walk home; play then continues.

chapters.title: Leave no opponents active to win
chapters.text: Later, all slate players have been sent to rescue. With nobody left in their half, white wins the round.

chapters.title: Reset all players for another round
chapters.text: Release both rescue zones, share the balls and rotate starting sides.

chapters.title: Put one keeper in each goal area
chapters.text: Two teams stay on their halves. Each keeper has a low-held noodle and a wide cone goal to defend.

chapters.title: Ordinary low hits still put you out
chapters.text: A direct hit below the waist sends A2 to waiting. Floor-bounced hits do not count.

chapters.title: The noodle stops a rolling ball
chapters.text: White recovers the ball and rolls toward goal. The keeper blocks with the noodle held low; noodle contact alone does not eliminate the keeper.

chapters.title: A clean catch eliminates the thrower
chapters.text: B2 collects the blocked ball, then throws. A3 catches the live throw, so B2 goes out; the keeper stays active.

chapters.title: Send a low ball through the goal
chapters.text: The keeper misses this roll. It passes below knee height through the goal and scores white one point.

chapters.title: A point ends this short round
chapters.text: Everyone returns after a goal or a full-team elimination. No one waits through the next point.

chapters.title: Rotate keepers and keep the score
chapters.text: Choose fresh keepers and share the balls evenly. The first team to three points wins.

chapters.title: Secretly choose one medic per team
chapters.text: The host knows both medics. Our teaching diagram marks them M so you can see how healing works.

chapters.title: A hit makes you stationary
chapters.text: A direct low hit or dropped catch makes you stay at your current spot. You do not leave the court.

chapters.title: Stationary does not mean unable to play
chapters.text: A2 picks up the ball without leaving the spot, then hits B2. Stationary players can catch and throw; a catch makes its thrower stationary.

chapters.title: A moving medic can restore you
chapters.text: The white medic touches A2’s shoulder. A2 can move again immediately.

chapters.title: A hit medic loses the healing power
chapters.text: Stationary B2 hits the medic. The medic now stays planted and cannot heal anyone, including themselves, although they can still catch and throw.

chapters.title: Stop at full freeze or five minutes
chapters.text: Here five minutes end with moving players on both teams: a draw. Making the entire opposing team stationary wins earlier.

chapters.title: Reset and choose different medics
chapters.text: Everyone moves again. Quietly give the medic jobs to new players before restarting.

chapters.title: Start with a hand on the wall
chapters.text: Everyone begins inside a safe pit. Keep the entry and exit clear. A host drops the ball into the centre.

chapters.title: Wait for the third bounce
chapters.text: Call “ga, ga, go” on three bounces. Play begins on “go”.

chapters.title: Strike with an open hand
chapters.text: Player 1 strikes the ball along the floor. Its below-knee contact puts player 3 out—even an own hit would count.

chapters.title: A clean airborne catch reverses it
chapters.text: Player 1 reaches the loose ball and strikes it airborne. Player 2 catches it, so the last hitter, player 1, leaves the pit.

chapters.title: Over the wall means a pause
chapters.text: Player 2 sends the ball outside. As the last toucher, player 2 is out. Pause, retrieve the ball and restart with three bounces.

chapters.title: The last player remaining wins
chapters.text: After the three-bounce restart, player 4 strikes a low ball that catches player 5. Player 4 is the last one in.

chapters.title: Bring everyone back
chapters.text: All players return for a new short round. Begin again with a hand on the wall and three bounces.

chapters.title: Give each team one square
chapters.text: Four teams begin with equal balls. Players must remain within their own square during play.

chapters.title: A direct low hit eliminates
chapters.text: A1 hits D1 below the waist. D1 waits beyond the court; a floor bounce would make the hit dead.

chapters.title: A catch puts the thrower out
chapters.text: A2 catches B1’s live throw. B1 leaves the court. This version does not rescue anyone for a catch.

chapters.title: A team is out when its square empties
chapters.text: C1 collects a loose ball entering the square and hits D2. Team D has nobody active, while the other teams keep playing.

chapters.title: Stop at one team or three minutes
chapters.text: The last active team wins. Here three minutes expire while several teams remain, so call a draw.

chapters.title: Return all four teams
chapters.text: Everyone goes back to their original square and balls are shared evenly for the next short round.

chapters.title: Place two pins near each back line
chapters.text: Protect your two pins without holding or moving them. All throws come from your own half.

chapters.title: Ordinary hits create waiting players
chapters.text: A direct below-waist hit sends A2 out. Bounced hits do not count.

chapters.title: A fallen pin rescues your team
chapters.text: A1 collects the loose ball and topples slate’s first pin. Every eliminated white player returns, including A2. Leave the pin down.

chapters.title: A catch has no rescue bonus
chapters.text: The loose ball rolls back across centre. A1 throws again, but B1 catches: A1 goes out, and no waiting player returns.

chapters.title: The second pin stays a live target
chapters.text: B1 returns a throw that bounces dead. A2 collects it, topples the other slate pin and rescues white’s waiting players again.

chapters.title: Two fallen opposing pins wins
chapters.text: White wins immediately. Eliminating every opposing player would also end the round.

chapters.title: Rebuild for a new round
chapters.text: Stand up all four pins, return all players and distribute the balls again.

chapters.title: Build two castles per team
chapters.text: Each castle uses one flat hoop, four leaning sides and one top hoop. Practise stable builds before adding balls.

chapters.title: Throw to topple a castle
chapters.text: A1 throws from the white half and knocks down a slate castle. White scores one point.

chapters.title: Body hits do not eliminate players
chapters.text: This throw touches B3, who stays active. Players may block or catch, but nobody crosses centre.

chapters.title: Rebuild during the action
chapters.text: Slate rebuilds its fallen castle while other players continue. Rebuilding restores a target; it does not erase the point already scored.

chapters.title: Both teams keep scoring topples
chapters.text: A slate throw knocks down a white castle. Slate adds one point; players remain active on both sides.

chapters.title: Compare scores at five minutes
chapters.text: Call the stop and compare how many castles each team toppled. This example is tied at one each.

chapters.title: Rebuild before the next round
chapters.text: Put every castle upright again. Reset scores and start a fresh timed round.

chapters.title: Choose a president on each team
chapters.text: Presidents are marked P. They may dodge within their half but do not throw. Their teammates are guards.

chapters.title: Guards can be eliminated normally
chapters.text: A direct below-waist hit sends guard A2 to waiting. Bounced balls are dead.

chapters.title: A guard’s catch has two effects
chapters.text: B1 recovers the loose ball and throws again. A1 catches it: B1 goes out and waiting teammate A2 returns.

chapters.title: The president can dodge too
chapters.text: The slate president moves to a new gap. Guards defend without grabbing or surrounding the president with contact.

chapters.title: One legal president hit wins
chapters.text: A1’s below-waist throw hits the slate president. The round ends immediately, even though slate still has active guards.

chapters.title: Rotate presidents and start again
chapters.text: Reset every guard and choose new presidents. If three minutes pass without a president hit, call a draw and rotate anyway.

chapters.title: Give each team a lane behind the opponents
chapters.text: The outside lanes belong to the opposite-side teams. A two-metre no-throw buffer separates each lane from active court.

chapters.title: A hit moves you to your outside lane
chapters.text: A2 is hit below the waist and moves behind slate. The player is still on the white team, and stays outside for this round.

chapters.title: Outside players can collect and pass
chapters.text: A2 collects a loose ball and passes it to A1. Outside players are not spectators.

chapters.title: Outside players can throw at opponents
chapters.text: A2’s next throw hits B2 from behind. B2 moves to the slate outside lane behind white.

chapters.title: Catching does not bring anyone inside
chapters.text: B1 catches A1’s live throw safely. No one is eliminated for this catch, and A2 and B2 stay outside.

chapters.title: An empty inside team loses
chapters.text: Later, the other white players are also hit and move outside. White has nobody left inside, so slate wins.

chapters.title: Return everyone and switch sides
chapters.text: All players return inside. Swap starting halves and assign the outside lanes behind the new opponents.

chapters.title: Everyone begins as a moving sprout
chapters.text: There are no teams. Use two or three soft balls; a holder has at most three steps and five seconds before throwing.

chapters.title: Remember the player who got you
chapters.text: Player 1 hits player 2. Player 2 becomes a stationary seed who cannot handle balls, and remembers player 1.

chapters.title: A catch can bring someone else back
chapters.text: Player 3 catches player 1’s live throw. Player 1 becomes a seed, so player 2 immediately sprouts again.

chapters.title: A different throw creates a new link
chapters.text: Player 2 hits player 4. Player 4 waits as a seed and remembers player 2; player 1 is still waiting for player 3.

chapters.title: The next hit releases that seed
chapters.text: Player 3 hits player 2. Player 4 returns because the person who got them has just become a seed.

chapters.title: One catch can release several sprouts
chapters.text: Player 4 catches player 3’s throw. Player 3 becomes a seed, so both players 1 and 2 return: player 3 had got them both.

chapters.title: Stop at one sprout or the timer
chapters.text: A sole moving sprout wins, but revivals can keep the round going. Here the timer ends; reset every seed.

chapters.title: Make the money ball unmistakable
chapters.text: Use a larger soft ball for the money ball. Ordinary balls retain their normal hit and catch rules.

chapters.title: An ordinary catch is only an out
chapters.text: B2 catches A1’s ordinary ball. A1 waits; ordinary-ball catches never revive teammates or win immediately.

chapters.title: The money ball cannot be hoarded
chapters.text: A2 controls the money ball. Throw it across centre within five seconds; deliberately rolling it eliminates the thrower.

chapters.title: A money-ball hit has two effects
chapters.text: A2 legally hits B3 below the waist. B3 goes out, and one waiting white player returns.

chapters.title: The other team prepares its throw
chapters.text: Slate recovers the money ball. B1 has the same five-second deadline and the same risk of a catch.

chapters.title: A money-ball catch wins immediately
chapters.text: A3 catches B1’s live money-ball throw. White wins at once, even with other slate players still active.

chapters.title: Return everyone for the next round
chapters.text: Reset all players and balls. Eliminating the whole opposing team is the other way to win.

chapters.title: Separate the roller from the dodgers
chapters.text: Mark a wide dodging strip and a rolling line a few metres away. One roller begins with the ball.

chapters.title: Roll along the floor at the feet
chapters.text: Dodgers move sideways inside the strip. A below-waist rolling hit sends player 2 to waiting; a high throw would not count.

chapters.title: Pause while retrieving the ball
chapters.text: Nobody starts the next roll yet. Retrieve the ball and wait until every dodger is ready.

chapters.title: Restart only when everyone is ready
chapters.text: The next low roll catches player 3. Players 1 and 4 keep dodging sideways in their strip.

chapters.title: The final remaining dodger wins
chapters.text: After retrieval, another low roll catches player 1. Player 4 is the last dodger in the strip.

chapters.title: Give the winner a new job
chapters.text: Player 4 becomes the roller. All waiting players and the previous roller return as dodgers.

chapters.title: Two teams, ten tokens each
chapters.text: This lesson follows white’s ten tokens. Each team has a bowl behind its line; a bottle stands halfway between them.

chapters.title: Knock the bottle down
chapters.text: A white throw topples the bottle. Only a hit starts the token relay.

chapters.title: Bank one token
chapters.text: One white runner carries one token to the bowl. Meanwhile slate races to the bottle and ball.

chapters.title: Return and tag the next
chapters.text: The first runner returns and tags the second. Slate stands the bottle and collects the ball, but must still get everybody behind its line.

chapters.title: Everyone back: “Stop!”
chapters.text: Slate has the ball, an upright bottle and everyone behind its line. Stop the relay. The unbanked carried token returns to the supply.

chapters.title: A miss earns no relay
chapters.text: Slate throws next and misses. Nobody moves tokens; the bottle is already upright.

chapters.title: Rotate throwers and repeat
chapters.text: White keeps its banked token and rotates throwers. The first team with all ten banked after a stop call wins.

chapters.title: Five kubbs on each baseline
chapters.text: The king stands in the middle. White begins with six underarm, end-over-end baton throws from its baseline.

chapters.title: A baseline kubb falls
chapters.text: White knocks over one slate kubb. Finish the six-throw turn before slate replies. Never hit the king this early.

chapters.title: Throw fallen kubbs back in
chapters.text: Before throwing batons, slate tosses its fallen kubb into white’s half. Stand it where it lands: it is now a field kubb.

chapters.title: Clear the field kubb first
chapters.text: Slate must knock down this field kubb before attacking baseline kubbs. Surviving field kubbs would let white advance its next throwing line.

chapters.title: Then clear the baseline
chapters.text: Continue through later turns. Here slate has finally cleared every white kubb. The king is now its legal final target.

chapters.title: Return to the original baseline
chapters.text: The king shot comes from slate’s original baseline. Topple it now to win; toppling it before clearing the opposing kubbs loses immediately.

chapters.title: Twelve pins and one thrower
chapters.text: Players take turns throwing the wooden pin underarm. The twelve numbered targets start together and will spread across the field.

chapters.title: Exactly one falls: score its number
chapters.text: Only pin twelve falls fully. A scores twelve, even though just one pin fell.

chapters.title: Stand it where it fell
chapters.text: Return pin twelve upright at its new position. Do not rebuild the original cluster. B takes the next throw.

chapters.title: Several fall: score the count
chapters.text: B knocks down three pins. That scores three, regardless of the numbers printed on those pins.

chapters.title: Keep the spread-out targets
chapters.text: Stand each fallen pin where it stopped and keep adding scores. In this later example, A has reached forty-seven.

chapters.title: Above fifty resets to twenty-five
chapters.text: A knocks down only pin eight. Forty-seven plus eight is fifty-five, so A’s total resets to twenty-five.

chapters.title: Exactly fifty wins
chapters.text: Retrieve the thrower for a winning example: B has forty-four and topples only six, reaching fifty exactly. Three consecutive scoreless throws eliminate a player.

chapters.title: Throw from one shared circle
chapters.text: Singles uses three boules each. Keep both feet grounded in the circle during a throw. The jack is the small target ball.

chapters.title: Jack, then the first boule
chapters.text: White throws the jack six to ten metres, then sends its first boule near it.

chapters.title: Farther away means play again
chapters.text: Slate’s first boule finishes farther from the jack. Slate must throw again; turns do not simply alternate.

chapters.title: Become closest: switch the turn
chapters.text: Slate’s second boule is now closer than white’s first. White must play until closer or out of boules.

chapters.title: Count only the closer team
chapters.text: After all six boules, two white boules lie inside the distance of slate’s nearest. White scores two; slate scores zero.

chapters.title: The scoring team starts again
chapters.text: Make the next throwing circle near the old jack. White starts the new end. Continue until a team reaches thirteen.

chapters.title: Four balls per team
chapters.text: Eight large balls share a narrow lane. White starts with the small pallino.

chapters.title: Roll into the far half
chapters.text: White rolls the pallino beyond halfway, then rolls its first ball towards it.

chapters.title: Slate is farther away
chapters.text: Slate’s first ball finishes farther from the pallino. Slate keeps rolling until it gets closer or runs out of balls.

chapters.title: Now white must play
chapters.text: Slate’s second ball becomes the nearest. White now has to improve its position.

chapters.title: A ball can move another
chapters.text: White uses its remaining balls. The last roll displaces slate’s close ball; contact is part of the game.

chapters.title: Finish all eight, then measure
chapters.text: Slate rolls its last two. Two white balls are nearer than slate’s nearest: two points to white only.

chapters.title: Reverse direction for the next end
chapters.text: The scoring team begins again from the other end. First to twelve wins this starter game.

chapters.title: Four bags each, one far board
chapters.text: Opponents alternate underarm throws towards the board at the other end. Finish all eight bags before scoring.

chapters.title: Through the hole scores three
chapters.text: White’s first bag goes through the hole: three potential round points.

chapters.title: On the board scores one
chapters.text: Slate’s bag rests on the board: one point. A ground-first bag scores zero and is removed.

chapters.title: Alternate until every bag settles
chapters.text: The remaining throws leave white with five and slate with four: white has one hole and two board bags; slate has one hole and one board bag.

chapters.title: Cancel the smaller score
chapters.text: Subtract slate’s four from white’s five. Only one point is added to white’s running total.

chapters.title: Play back from the other end
chapters.text: Collect the bags and throw towards the other board. White scored, so white starts. First to twenty-one or more after a round wins; there is no bust.

chapters.title: Partners stand at opposite goals
chapters.text: Each pair has a thrower and a redirecting partner. The partner may touch the disc once, without catching or carrying it.

chapters.title: Deflect onto the outside: one
chapters.text: The partner redirects the throw into the outside of the goal. This assisted outside hit scores one.

chapters.title: Hit directly: two
chapters.text: Return the disc and compare another throw: it hits the outside with no partner touch. This direct outside hit scores two.

chapters.title: Deflect inside: three
chapters.text: Return the disc, then the partner redirects a fresh throw into the goal. An assisted entry scores three. A ground-first throw scores zero.

chapters.title: Both partners throw once
chapters.text: The partner throws back towards the other goal. After both partners have thrown once, the opposing pair takes its team turn.

chapters.title: An overshoot subtracts the throw
chapters.text: Exactly twenty-one is required. At twenty, a three-point throw would overshoot, so subtract three: the total becomes seventeen. Complete equal team turns.

chapters.title: Direct entry wins immediately
chapters.text: Collect the disc. A fresh shot goes through the slot unassisted and stays inside: an immediate win, regardless of score. An unassisted top entry also wins.

chapters.title: Three rungs, three values
chapters.text: The top rung is three points, middle two, bottom one. Each side has three bolas and takes all three throws before the other side.

chapters.title: White throws all three
chapters.text: White leaves one bola on top and two on the middle. Do not score or remove them yet.

chapters.title: Slate can knock one off
chapters.text: Slate’s top-rung throw dislodges white’s top bola. Slate also lands one on the bottom and misses one. Knocked-off bolas no longer count.

chapters.title: Count what is still hanging
chapters.text: White has two middle bolas: four. Slate has top plus bottom: four. This starter version adds both totals, with no bonuses or cancellation.

chapters.title: Discard a round that overshoots
chapters.text: Later example: white’s nineteen plus four exceeds twenty-one, so white stays on nineteen. Slate’s seventeen plus four reaches exactly twenty-one.

chapters.title: Complete the round, then declare it
chapters.text: Slate wins after the complete round. Clear the frame. Alternate the starting side; if both reach twenty-one together, play another round.

chapters.title: Three washers per side
chapters.text: Opponents alternate tossing towards the far box. Finish all six washers before working out the score.

chapters.title: Inside the cup scores three
chapters.text: White’s washer finishes inside the centre cup. It is worth three round points.

chapters.title: Elsewhere in the box scores one
chapters.text: Slate’s washer lands inside the box but outside its cup: one round point. Outside the box is zero.

chapters.title: Finish the alternating throws
chapters.text: White adds one box washer and misses once. Slate’s other two miss. The settled round totals are four for white and one for slate.

chapters.title: Subtract the lower score
chapters.text: Four minus one leaves three. Add three to white’s running total; slate adds nothing.

chapters.title: Play back towards the other box
chapters.text: Collect washers and reverse direction. The scoring side starts. First to twenty-one or more after a round wins.

chapters.title: Everyone aims at the same hoop
chapters.text: This example begins at hoop one from its marked playing side. The stroke order is always blue, red, black, yellow.

chapters.title: Blue takes one stroke
chapters.text: Blue approaches the current hoop. That uses its turn; red plays next.

chapters.title: A hit gives no extra stroke
chapters.text: Red hits blue’s ball away. Contact is allowed, but red gets no bonus stroke. Black is still next.

chapters.title: Completely through earns one
chapters.text: Black passes completely through the hoop from the correct side. Blue and black’s team earns one point.

chapters.title: Next hoop, same ball positions
chapters.text: Everyone now contests the next hoop. Yellow’s stroke goes out; replace its ball where it crossed the boundary. Other balls stay where they stopped.

chapters.title: Keep the colour order
chapters.text: Blue plays again, then red. Follow the source’s twelve-hoop route. First to seven points wins; at six-all, contest hoop three again.

chapters.title: Start at the marked tee
chapters.text: Choose tees, baskets and boundaries before playing. Everyone throws one at a time from this tee.

chapters.title: Each first throw counts one
chapters.text: A and B take their first throws. Their landing places become their next throwing positions. B is farther from the basket.

chapters.title: The farther player throws next
chapters.text: B throws from the previous landing place, not from the tee. B has now used two throws.

chapters.title: Out adds one penalty
chapters.text: A’s second throw crosses the boundary. Add one penalty, making three strokes. Resume just inside where the disc last crossed out.

chapters.title: Continue from the new lie
chapters.text: A is farther away, so A throws again from the boundary lie. This approach makes A’s count four.

chapters.title: Every finishing throw still counts
chapters.text: B finishes in three. A then finishes in five, including the penalty. A disc must finish in the basket for this hole to end.

chapters.title: Record and move together
chapters.text: Record both hole totals, then move to the next tee. Lowest combined throw count across the agreed course wins.

chapters.title: Build one five-block figure
chapters.text: Both sides play the same agreed figure. This example starts with a row. Use soft practice pieces and a clear throwing area.

chapters.title: Take the first underarm throw
chapters.text: The baton scatters the row. Several blocks move outside, but a block’s centre crossing the line is not enough.

chapters.title: Count only fully cleared blocks
chapters.text: Three blocks are completely outside. One still overlaps the square’s edge and one remains inside. Leave them where they stopped.

chapters.title: Use the second throw
chapters.text: The second baton clears the last two pieces completely. A used two throws for this figure.

chapters.title: Rebuild identically for the opponent
chapters.text: Record two throws for A. Rebuild the same row for B; each turn allows two baton throws, repeating as needed until the square is empty.

chapters.title: Repeat with the cross
chapters.text: After both sides finish the row, play the same agreed cross figure. Record every throw used.

chapters.title: Then play the five-block well
chapters.text: Finish the short game with the well. Add each side’s throws across all three figures; the smaller total wins.

chapters.title: One chaser, three runners
chapters.text: This small example has four seated chasers facing alternate sides. One teammate chases; three opponents run.

chapters.title: The runner crosses the lane
chapters.text: Runners may cross. The active chaser cannot cross or reverse direction except around an end cone.

chapters.title: Tap a back: “Kho!”
chapters.text: The chaser taps a seated teammate’s back, calls “kho” and takes their seat. That teammate starts on the side they face.

chapters.title: A gentle tag scores one
chapters.text: The new chaser reaches runner 1. A gentle tag scores one; that runner leaves this batch.

chapters.title: Finish the batch
chapters.text: After the other two runners are tagged, all three are out. The chasing team has three points.

chapters.title: Send the next three
chapters.text: A fresh batch enters. Keep chasing and handing over until the five-minute turn ends.

chapters.title: Now exchange roles
chapters.text: Slate chases; white runs. Give both teams equal time. The side with more tags wins.

chapters.title: Tags replace tackles
chapters.text: This is the tag-belt adaptation. Teams stay in their halves until one raider crosses; every player begins with a removable tag.

chapters.title: One raider enters
chapters.text: White sends one raider across. They have up to twenty seconds to collect tags and return.

chapters.title: Take a defender’s tag
chapters.text: The raider removes slate 1’s tag. It is only a potential point until the raider gets back home.

chapters.title: Cross home to score
chapters.text: The raider returns safely. One collected tag becomes one point. All tags are returned after the raid.

chapters.title: The other team raids
chapters.text: Now slate sends one raider into white’s half. Teams alternate and rotate who raids.

chapters.title: Lose your tag, lose the raid
chapters.text: White removes the raider’s tag before they return. White gets one defence point. Timeout or stepping out has the same result.

chapters.title: Reset tags and take turns
chapters.text: Restore every tag. After equal numbers of raids, the higher total wins. There is no tackling, holding or contact blocking.

chapters.title: Stack seven discs
chapters.text: White attacks from the throwing line. Slate fields. The attackers have up to three throws total to topple the stack.

chapters.title: One hit starts the scramble
chapters.text: The stack falls. Attackers can now rebuild while defenders recover the ball. Three missed opening throws would swap the roles.

chapters.title: Rebuild while they retrieve
chapters.text: Two attackers replace three discs. Slate retrieves the ball and can pass it between fielders.

chapters.title: A low hit puts one out
chapters.text: Slate passes and gently hits attacker 1 below the knees. That player leaves this round; the other attackers keep rebuilding.

chapters.title: Seven discs: “Lagori!”
chapters.text: The remaining attackers complete all seven and call “Lagori!” White scores one. If every attacker were out first, slate would score.

chapters.title: Reset and swap roles
chapters.text: Rebuild the starting tower and swap attackers and fielders. Play six rounds with equal attacking turns; most points wins.

chapters.title: Start behind the baseline
chapters.text: Play singles here. Each side has one open-hand strike to return the peteca; there are no teammate passes.

chapters.title: Serve with an open hand
chapters.text: White strikes the peteca from behind the baseline. The shuttle crosses the net into slate’s court.

chapters.title: Return it with one strike
chapters.text: Slate returns it immediately with one open-hand strike. Catching, double touches and failed returns lose the rally.

chapters.title: Land it inside the court
chapters.text: White sends the next strike into an empty corner. The peteca lands inside slate’s court: one point to white.

chapters.title: The rally winner serves
chapters.text: Reset the shuttle behind white’s baseline. In these starter rules, the side that won the rally serves next.

chapters.title: Win a short set
chapters.text: Continue to eleven with a two-point lead; 11–9 is one winning example. Change ends during the set and win two sets for the match.

chapters.title: Three players on each side
chapters.text: The server stands on the service mark. A teammate supplies the toss. Use feet, legs, torso or head; hands and arms cannot touch the ball.

chapters.title: Toss to the server
chapters.text: The teammate tosses to the server. The server kicks this ball over the net to start the rally.

chapters.title: Kick it across
chapters.text: White’s serve travels into slate’s court. Slate now has up to three touches to return it.

chapters.title: First touch keeps it up
chapters.text: Slate 1 lifts the ball with a foot towards teammate 2. Count one touch.

chapters.title: Second touch sets it
chapters.text: Slate 2 raises the ball towards teammate 3. Count two. One player may also take multiple touches.

chapters.title: Third touch goes over
chapters.text: Slate 3 returns it across. A fourth touch would lose the point; three is the limit.

chapters.title: Grounded ball: slate scores
chapters.text: The ball lands in white’s court. Slate gains one and serves next: serving teams alternate after every point. Win two sets; sets are to fifteen, or seventeen after 14–14.

chapters.title: Two roles, three zones
chapters.text: This teaching adaptation has seven pou outside. Kīoma stay outside except two central guards; Taniwha have two inner players and outside teammates.

chapters.title: Touch one new pou
chapters.text: A Kīoma carrier touches a pou with the ball: one pending point. Touching this same post again adds nothing.

chapters.title: A different pou adds one
chapters.text: Kīoma travel outside to another post. Two different pou now mean two pending points; they have not yet been banked.

chapters.title: Carry in and ground
chapters.text: The scoring carrier crosses the inner ring and grounds centrally, banking both points. No passing during the crossing. A lost tag or ball would erase the pending total.

chapters.title: Opponents restart outside
chapters.text: After either side scores, the other side restarts at the outer edge. Pending pou points reset to zero.

chapters.title: Pass to an inner player
chapters.text: Taniwha pass from outside to an inner shooter. Kīoma’s two central guards may block or catch without touching the barrel.

chapters.title: Hit the tupu for one
chapters.text: The shot hits the central target: one Taniwha point. Kīoma restart outside. Swap roles every five minutes and compare totals after equal time.

chapters.title: Clear the hitting area
chapters.text: The short lippa rests on a base with one tapered end exposed. Only the hitter is in front of the waiting line.

chapters.title: Tap the tapered end
chapters.text: The long bat taps one end. The short stick lifts into the air.

chapters.title: Strike it while airborne
chapters.text: Strike the lifted stick away. Everybody waits until it lands and stops. A complete miss still uses an attempt.

chapters.title: Measure whole bat-lengths
chapters.text: Measure from the base to the stopped stick. This throw reaches four whole bat-lengths; the short remainder adds nothing.

chapters.title: Retrieve only on the signal
chapters.text: The leader gives the signal after measuring. The hitter retrieves the stick; the next attempt starts from the same base.

chapters.title: Five attempts, then the next player
chapters.text: An example five-throw total is eighteen. Give every player five attempts; the highest combined distance wins.

chapters.title: Two targets, two batters
chapters.text: A batter defends each target. A grounded bat inside its base makes that batter safe. Fielders bowl from behind the opposite ends.

chapters.title: Bowl at the far target
chapters.text: Slate bowls the soft ball towards the right-hand target. Its batter tries to hit the ball away.

chapters.title: Hit away, then decide to run
chapters.text: The batter sends the ball into space. Fielders chase it; the batters may now exchange ends.

chapters.title: One exchange scores one
chapters.text: Both batters reach the opposite bases and ground their bats. This completed exchange scores one run in the teaching adaptation.

chapters.title: An exposed target can fall
chapters.text: On another attempted exchange, a fielder knocks over an unprotected target. Batting and fielding roles must switch; an airborne catch also switches them.

chapters.title: The other pair bats
chapters.text: Reset the targets. Slate now bats and white fields. Continue until one pair completes its tenth run.

chapters.title: Choose opposite scoring roles
chapters.text: A scores for matching feet; B scores for different feet. The L and R labels refer to each player’s own left and right.

chapters.title: Clap on one shared beat
chapters.text: Clap together so both players make their choice at the same moment.

chapters.title: Make a small jump
chapters.text: Jump together. Each player chooses one foot to put forward when landing.

chapters.title: Both choose left: a match
chapters.text: Both land with their own left foot forward. The feet match, so A earns one point. Both choosing right would also match.

chapters.title: Left and right: different
chapters.text: On the next beat, A chooses left and B chooses right. The feet differ, so B earns one point.

chapters.title: Reach ten, then switch roles
chapters.text: Repeat until one player reaches ten. Swap matching and different scoring roles for the next game; groups can then rotate partners.

chapters.title: Hide one token per player
chapters.text: The leader hides three tokens while these three searchers wait out of sight. Everybody then gathers behind the shared start-and-finish line.

chapters.title: “Pilolo!” means search
chapters.text: The leader calls “Pilolo!” Searchers enter the agreed area, each looking for one token.

chapters.title: Find one, then go home
chapters.text: A finds a token. Take just one and head back; never take a token from another player.

chapters.title: Cross the line carrying it
chapters.text: A crosses the finish line with the token first and wins this round. B has also found one and is returning.

chapters.title: Let everyone finish
chapters.text: B and C complete their searches and return with one token each. Keep the round open until everyone finishes.

chapters.title: Change the leader and hide again
chapters.text: A becomes the next leader. Hide the tokens again. Play five rounds and count first finishes, or celebrate each round separately.

chapters.title: A circle shares one shuttle
chapters.text: This is a cooperative keep-up circle. Everyone has room to lift a leg. Count successful contacts together.

chapters.title: Kick upward to start
chapters.text: A drops the jianzi towards a foot and kicks it up. The first successful contact makes the count one.

chapters.title: Pass with another foot touch
chapters.text: B keeps the shuttle airborne and directs it towards C. That is contact two. Hands and arms cannot help.

chapters.title: A knee can keep it alive
chapters.text: C lifts the shuttle with a knee towards D. Count three; feet are not the only legal body part.

chapters.title: The floor ends this rally
chapters.text: The shuttle falls before D returns it. The rally ends at three; record three as the group’s current best.

chapters.title: Start from zero with someone new
chapters.text: B starts the next rally at zero. Keep the best score and try to beat it before the five-minute session ends.

chapters.title: Safe boxes at opposite ends
chapters.text: White runs and slate fields. The roller calls one runner into the kicking area. Only the end boxes are safe.

chapters.title: Call a name and roll
chapters.text: The roller calls runner 1 and rolls the ball towards them. They must kick it beyond halfway.

chapters.title: Kick long and run
chapters.text: The kick passes halfway, so runner 1 must cross. Runner 2 chooses to join. Missed or short kicks retry; three failures dismiss the kicker.

chapters.title: Reach the far safe box
chapters.text: Runner 1 reaches safety and scores one crossing in this adaptation. Slate retrieves the ball while runner 2 is still exposed.

chapters.title: A low hit outside puts you out
chapters.text: The fielder gently throws below runner 2’s knees. That runner leaves this innings; a runner already inside the safe box cannot be put out.

chapters.title: Everyone safe or out: restart
chapters.text: The action stops once everyone is safe or out. The roller calls the next runner; keep the completed crossing on the scoreboard.

chapters.title: Give each team an innings
chapters.text: Swap after five minutes or when everyone is out. Give equal innings; the team with more completed crossings wins.

chapters.title: Two frames, either end
chapters.text: Both teams may shoot at either frame. The marked semicircles are not scoring landing areas. This drawing uses a small example.

chapters.title: Pass without interference
chapters.text: Defenders do not intercept or block passes. Hold for at most three seconds, take at most three steps, and shoot within three team passes.

chapters.title: Shoot, then watch the rebound
chapters.text: White shoots at the left frame. The rebound is still live: slate can catch it before it lands outside the semicircle.

chapters.title: A catch changes the attack
chapters.text: Slate catches the rebound. There is no point. Slate now attacks, with the same passing and shooting limits.

chapters.title: An uncaught rebound scores
chapters.text: Slate shoots at the other frame. This rebound lands in court outside its semicircle, so slate scores one.

chapters.title: The conceding team restarts
chapters.text: White restarts behind that baseline. After three consecutive shots at one frame, the next shot must use the other frame.

chapters.title: A bad landing rewards opponents
chapters.text: A shot landing inside the semicircle gives opponents one point. Missing the frame or rebounding out does too. A dropped pass instead changes possession.

chapters.title: Three teams surround one ball
chapters.text: Each colour has four players. Three white players support the ball; the fourth prepares to hit.

chapters.title: Call before the hit
chapters.text: The hitter calls “Omnikin” and another team’s colour. Only that called team must make the catch.

chapters.title: Send the ball outward
chapters.text: Hit outward or upward, never downward. This introduction requires at least three metres of travel. Give the called team room.

chapters.title: Catch, support, prepare again
chapters.text: Slate controls the ball before it lands. Slate’s players now support it and prepare their next hit. Rotate hitters within each team.

chapters.title: Choose the next receivers
chapters.text: Slate calls blue before sending the ball away. White and slate leave blue space to catch.

chapters.title: A miss scores for both rivals
chapters.text: The ball reaches the floor before blue controls it. White and slate each score one point.

chapters.title: The faulting team restarts
chapters.text: Blue supports the ball and starts again. After ten minutes, the highest score wins; a tie may stand.

chapters.title: Start behind the end-zone lines
chapters.text: Slate defends and holds the opening disc. White attacks the end zone at the right.

chapters.title: The defence throws the pull
chapters.text: Slate throws to white to start the point. White teammates spread out to offer passing options.

chapters.title: Catch, stop, and pivot
chapters.text: The holder cannot run with the disc. A nearby marker counts ten seconds aloud while teammates move into space.

chapters.title: Catch inside the end zone
chapters.text: White 3 catches a teammate’s pass inside the slate end zone. White scores one point.

chapters.title: Switch ends after each point
chapters.text: The scoring team now throws the next opening disc. Both teams change ends.

chapters.title: A failed pass changes possession
chapters.text: After the next pull, slate drops a pass. White takes possession immediately. Interceptions, out-of-bounds passes and a completed ten-count also turn it over.

chapters.title: Choose the unarmed runners
chapters.text: R marks each team’s runner. Spar players use inspected padded equipment for gentle tags below the shoulders. This introduction excludes chains, wrestling and pinning.

chapters.title: Runners collect the centre ball
chapters.text: On “Jugger!”, runners approach the ball. Only a runner may pick it up, carry it or place it in a goal.

chapters.title: A gentle tag pauses a player
chapters.text: A tagged spar player raises a hand and sits or kneels if comfortable. Count five audible beats, one-and-a-half seconds apart, before rejoining.

chapters.title: A tagged runner drops immediately
chapters.text: White’s runner is tagged and puts the ball down immediately. Nobody may grab a body or block a player with their body.

chapters.title: A runner places the ball
chapters.text: Slate’s active runner collects the loose ball and places it in white’s goal. Slate scores one. The five-beat player can now rejoin.

chapters.title: Reset everyone after a point
chapters.text: Return to the baselines with the ball at centre. Rotate runners. First to three points wins this introductory match.

chapters.title: Two pairs, one round net
chapters.text: The server faces the receiver. Leave clear space in every direction; there are no fixed sides after the serve.

chapters.title: Serve down onto the net
chapters.text: White strikes down onto the net. The rebound travels towards slate’s receiver.

chapters.title: Alternate your team’s touches
chapters.text: Slate 1 sends the ball to slate 2. These are touches one and two. Nobody catches or carries the ball.

chapters.title: Return by the third touch
chapters.text: Slate 2 sets to slate 1, who uses touch three to hit the net. White moves around it to receive. Give opponents room.

chapters.title: A ground touch ends the rally
chapters.text: White cannot return the ball before it lands. Slate scores one. Rim hits, double net bounces and too many touches also lose the rally.

chapters.title: The point winner serves
chapters.text: Slate serves next. Alternate your team’s server when regaining service. Play to eleven, winning by two.

chapters.title: Mark home and the far base
chapters.text: Choose batting order and a pitcher. Keep waiting players outside the bat area.

chapters.title: One swing, then run
chapters.text: The pitcher tosses underarm. After one swing, hit or miss, put the bat down and run to the far base.

chapters.title: The far base is safe
chapters.text: The runner reaches safety while a fielder retrieves the bounced ball. An airborne catch would put the batter out. The runner may wait at this base.

chapters.title: The pitcher can freeze play
chapters.text: The runner starts home. Fielders return the ball to the pitcher, who calls “Freeze”.

chapters.title: Return to the last safe base
chapters.text: In this version, the untagged runner returns to the far base. Wait until play is live to try again.

chapters.title: An out-and-back scores one
chapters.text: On a later live play, the runner commits to coming home and completes the return. That scores one run.

chapters.title: Fielders tag with ball in hand
chapters.text: The next runner is gently tagged between bases and is out. Never throw at runners. Three outs switch teams and clear waiting runners.

chapters.title: Spread out on each side
chapters.text: A low net divides the court. White’s server begins behind the back line.

chapters.title: Throw a serve over the net
chapters.text: Slate catches the serve before it lands. Newcomb uses catches and throws instead of volleyball contacts.

chapters.title: Stay where you catch
chapters.text: The catcher stays in place, with feet on the ground, and must throw back within three seconds. No blocking or spiking.

chapters.title: Return directly to opponents
chapters.text: Slate throws directly over the net. This starter version does not allow passes between teammates.

chapters.title: Make the return land inside
chapters.text: White catches, then returns into an empty part of slate’s court. It lands inside: white scores one. Drops, net throws and out-balls lose a point.

chapters.title: Serve after winning the point
chapters.text: White serves again. Rotate the server when your team gains service so everyone has a turn. First to eleven wins; nobody goes out.

chapters.title: Put catchers behind opposite lines
chapters.text: Each team has a catcher behind the far end line. The other players stay inside the court.

chapters.title: Pass and stay still
chapters.text: White 1 passes underarm to white 2. The holder stays still. Defenders can intercept passes, but cannot touch the holder or their held ball.

chapters.title: Include every court teammate
chapters.text: White 3 receives next. All three court players in this small example have now touched the ball, so a scoring pass becomes legal.

chapters.title: Find the end-line catcher
chapters.text: The catcher moves along the line while staying behind it. A caught legal pass scores one.

chapters.title: Rotate the catcher and restart
chapters.text: White rotates its catcher. Slate receives the restart and must include all its court players before scoring.

chapters.title: An interception turns it over
chapters.text: White intercepts a slate pass. White starts a new possession. Dropped passes and out-balls also give the opponents possession.

chapters.title: Ground balls use feet
chapters.text: Dribble or kick a ball on the ground. Nobody may simply pick it up. Cone goals and end zones offer different scoring routes.

chapters.title: Kick into a controlled catch
chapters.text: White lofts a controlled kick towards a teammate. The receiver must catch it before it touches the ground.

chapters.title: Now throwing is allowed
chapters.text: The airborne catch changes the ball to aerial play. The holder must pass, shoot or drop within three seconds or three steps.

chapters.title: An end-zone catch scores one
chapters.text: White 3 catches a teammate’s pass in the opposing end zone. White scores one.

chapters.title: Opponents restart at centre
chapters.text: Slate takes a free pass at centre after the score.

chapters.title: A drop restores feet-only play
chapters.text: Slate drops the aerial ball. It is a ground ball again immediately; slate must now kick it.

chapters.title: A ground goal scores three
chapters.text: Slate kicks the ground ball between the opposing goal cones. Slate scores three, then white restarts at centre.

chapters.title: Assign halves and matched defenders
chapters.text: A full team has four attackers in one half and four defenders in the other. This small drawing shows the roles, with agreed defending pairs.

chapters.title: Recognise a defended shot
chapters.text: Slate A faces white A, stands between player and basket, is within arm’s reach, and actively blocks. All four conditions matter.

chapters.title: A defended basket does not score
chapters.text: White shoots anyway. Even though the ball goes through, a defended shot gives possession to the defence.

chapters.title: Pass to the attacking half
chapters.text: Slate passes towards its attackers. Players stay in their assigned halves and cannot run or dribble while holding the ball.

chapters.title: An undefended basket scores one
chapters.text: Slate’s attacker shoots without a qualifying defender and scores. White receives a centre restart.

chapters.title: Count goals across both teams
chapters.text: On the next attack, white scores an undefended basket. There have now been two total goals: one by each team.

chapters.title: Swap halves after two goals
chapters.text: Both teams exchange attacking and defending halves after every two total goals. The conceding team restarts at centre.

chapters.title: Begin seated on a smooth court
chapters.text: The server waits behind the end line. In this introduction, keep part of your torso on the floor when playing the ball.

chapters.title: The serve may be blocked
chapters.text: White serves. Unlike standing volleyball, slate may block the serve at the net.

chapters.title: Move along the floor
chapters.text: Slate’s block sends the ball back. White moves along the floor to cover its landing path.

chapters.title: Use up to three contacts
chapters.text: White keeps the ball up with separate contacts. No catching or throwing; consecutive touches by one player are normally faults.

chapters.title: Every rally awards a point
chapters.text: White returns the ball into slate’s court, where it lands. White scores one. Faults and out-balls also award the opponents a point.

chapters.title: The point winner serves next
chapters.text: White serves next. Rotate the serving order when service changes teams. The introductory set ends at fifteen with a two-point lead.

chapters.title: Mark front and back halves
chapters.text: Use a comfortable net height and a light ball for this version. Divide both sides into front and back halves.

chapters.title: Throw the serve over
chapters.text: White serves from behind the back line. Slate catches it in the front half.

chapters.title: A front catch must go deep
chapters.text: Slate returns directly from the catch position into white’s back half. No running or passing to teammates.

chapters.title: A back catch has both options
chapters.text: White caught in the back half, so its return may reach either slate half. White chooses the front again.

chapters.title: A short front return is a fault
chapters.text: Slate catches in front but returns into white’s front half. That is too short: white scores one. Drops, net throws and out-balls also lose points.

chapters.title: Rotate the rally winner’s server
chapters.text: White won the rally and serves. Rotate its server after this point. Play to eleven with a two-point lead.

chapters.title: Link hands around the hoop
chapters.text: With everyone’s agreement, close the circle with a hoop around one joined pair of hands. Choose one direction.

chapters.title: Pass your body through
chapters.text: Person 2 carefully steps through the hoop. Neighbours lift or lower their joined hands to help; nobody pulls anyone through.

chapters.title: Keep the hand chain intact
chapters.text: The hoop is now between people 2 and 3. It moves along the existing hand link, ready for person 3.

chapters.title: Comfort comes before the chain
chapters.text: If someone needs to release a grip, pause. Nobody is eliminated and there is no penalty for stopping.

chapters.title: Reconnect and continue together
chapters.text: Restore a comfortable link and continue in the same direction. The hoop passes people 3 and 4.

chapters.title: Return to the starting link
chapters.text: After people 5, 6 and 1 pass through, the hoop returns to its original link. The whole group succeeds.

chapters.title: Make the next circuit smoother
chapters.text: Discuss what helped. Reset comfortably and try a second circuit together. An opening hoop or agreed seated adaptation can change the movement.

chapters.title: Agree an order and freeze
chapters.text: Count down, take one step into a starting pose, then freeze. H marks a hand: only gentle taps to the back of a hand count.

chapters.title: One action, one possible dodge
chapters.text: Player 1 makes one continuous attempt. Only targeted player 2 may dodge once. The tap misses; both freeze in their new poses.

chapters.title: A hand tap ends that player’s round
chapters.text: Player 2 uses the next turn to tap player 3’s hand. Player 3 leaves this short round.

chapters.title: Keep the original turn order
chapters.text: Skip eliminated player 3. Player 4 acts next and taps player 1. Nobody else moves in response.

chapters.title: The last active player wins
chapters.text: Player 2 taps player 4’s hand. Only player 2 remains, so this round ends.

chapters.title: Everybody returns for another round
chapters.text: Everyone rejoins. Move the starting player one place around the original circle: player 2 starts the next round.

chapters.title: Learn the repeating sequence
chapters.text: Everyone can see one another. Practise a comfortable passing gesture and agree a target of thirty uninterrupted passes.

chapters.title: Send Zip to a clear receiver
chapters.text: Player 1 gestures to player 3 and says “Zip”. The receiver must know the gesture is for them.

chapters.title: The receiver sends Zap
chapters.text: Player 3 chooses player 6 and sends “Zap”. The direction is unpredictable, but the word order is fixed.

chapters.title: The next receiver sends Zop
chapters.text: Player 6 sends “Zop” to player 4. The next word must return to “Zip”.

chapters.title: Pause when the order breaks
chapters.text: Player 4 says the wrong word. Pause together. Nobody is eliminated. An unclear receiver also triggers a pause.

chapters.title: Restart with the last receiver
chapters.text: Player 4 restarts at “Zip” and sends it to player 5. Reset the uninterrupted count and work towards thirty together.

chapters.title: Begin in individual pairs
chapters.text: Introduce yourselves. Reveal rock, paper or scissors together on “shoot”. Replay ties until each pair has a winner.

chapters.title: The other player becomes a supporter
chapters.text: Players 1, 3, 5 and 7 win these example duels. Their partners remain involved as supporters.

chapters.title: Winners challenge other winners
chapters.text: Each winner finds another winner. Supporters follow at a comfortable distance and cheer without crowding.

chapters.title: Whole supporter groups transfer
chapters.text: Players 1 and 5 win. Players 3 and 7, together with their existing supporters, join the new winners. Only two competitors remain.

chapters.title: Play the final duel
chapters.text: Player 1 reveals paper; player 5 reveals rock. Paper wins. Both finalists have supporters around them.

chapters.title: Celebrate the whole group
chapters.text: Player 1 is this round’s rockstar. The other finalist and their supporters join in; everyone remains part of the event.

chapters.title: Restart from individual pairs
chapters.text: Mix partners so people meet someone new. Everyone becomes a competitor again.

chapters.title: Place popcorn in the centre
chapters.text: Everyone holds the edge comfortably, around waist height. Use soft, lightweight balls and agree a stop signal.

chapters.title: Shake together on Pop
chapters.text: Practise lifting and lowering together. On “Pop!”, bounce the fabric while keeping hold and staying in place.

chapters.title: Bounce balls over the edge
chapters.text: Two balls leave the parachute. Steer with the fabric rather than reaching in with your hands. Keep working on the remaining two.

chapters.title: The final ball ends the attempt
chapters.text: All four balls are off. Lower the parachute and stop moving it. The group has succeeded.

chapters.title: Collect only after stopping
chapters.text: With the parachute lowered and still, collect the balls. Nobody chases a ball while the group is still shaking.

chapters.title: Refill and try another rhythm
chapters.text: Return the balls to the centre. Try another round with a shared lifting rhythm or smaller comfortable movements.

chapters.title: Choose two different hand partners
chapters.text: Each person joins right hands with a non-neighbour, then left hands with a different non-neighbour. This six-person drawing shows the resulting connections.

chapters.title: Agree on one movement
chapters.text: Trace who is connected to whom. Suggest one slow movement at a time. Nobody should pull, twist or lift another person.

chapters.title: A facilitator may allow a cut
chapters.text: This example uses one of the two optional cuts. Players 5 and 2 briefly release their connection, with everyone’s agreement.

chapters.title: Move without changing partners
chapters.text: Use the opening to rearrange slowly. All the other hand partners stay connected. The drawing spreads the same connection chain into a loop.

chapters.title: Restore the exact same connection
chapters.text: Players 5 and 2 join hands again. A cut is a temporary release, not permission to choose different partners.

chapters.title: Recognise a workable ending
chapters.text: This knot becomes one loop. Some become several loops, and some cannot untangle safely. Explaining why is also a valid finish.

chapters.title: Release and make a fresh knot
chapters.text: Release all grips, discuss what helped, and start a fresh knot if everyone wants another round. Anyone may release immediately for discomfort.

chapters.title: Choose the order and first end
chapters.text: This example uses number cards. You could instead agree on birthday month and day, without the year, or another comfortable shared criterion.

chapters.title: Communicate without speech
chapters.text: Players gesture and move themselves into a line. Nobody pulls or pushes another person. Signing, writing or agreed aids can help.

chapters.title: Signal when the line is ready
chapters.text: When everyone believes the order is correct, signal completion together. Now it is time to check.

chapters.title: Read the values from one end
chapters.text: Read aloud: one, two, four, three, five. Four and three are reversed. The group can repair the line rather than starting over.

chapters.title: Return to gestures and repair
chapters.text: Players carrying three and four swap places using gestures. Check again: the whole line is now correctly ordered.

chapters.title: Choose a new challenge together
chapters.text: The group has completed one correct line. Try a new criterion or split into smaller groups for the next round.

chapters.title: Link only with everyone’s agreement
chapters.text: Float the balloon into the centre of a clear space. Agree a shared target, such as twenty touches.

chapters.title: Use a gentle first touch
chapters.text: Keep the balloon up using hands, arms or shoulders. Do not kick. Count every touch aloud.

chapters.title: Move the whole circle together
chapters.text: The balloon drifts right. Everyone adjusts while keeping the hand chain linked. After several touches, the count has reached seven.

chapters.title: A landing resets the count
chapters.text: The balloon reaches the floor. Pause and reset the count. A broken hand chain also means pausing and resetting.

chapters.title: Plan a better next attempt
chapters.text: Regroup comfortably. Discuss how to cover the drifting side, then float the balloon again with the count at zero.

chapters.title: Reach the group’s target
chapters.text: On a later attempt, the group reaches twenty touches. Celebrate the shared target, or use your previous best as the next challenge.

chapters.title: Begin with one soft object
chapters.text: A says someone’s name and checks they are ready before an underarm toss. Each receiver chooses someone who has not yet received.

chapters.title: Choose a new receiver each time
chapters.text: A sends to D, then D sends to B. No receiver repeats while the first circuit is being built.

chapters.title: Return to the starter
chapters.text: B sends to E, E to C, and C back to A. Everyone has received once. Repeat this exact order until the group remembers it.

chapters.title: Add a second object behind
chapters.text: Restart the same sequence, then introduce a second object behind the first. Both follow A–D–B–E–C–A.

chapters.title: Pause the dropped object’s journey
chapters.text: B drops the first object. Retrieve it and resume from B; do not restart it from A or change its next receiver.

chapters.title: Resume from the same player
chapters.text: B retrieves the object, then sends it to E. Check readiness before the toss; the original order stays intact.

chapters.title: Finish every object’s circuit
chapters.text: Continue the same order until both objects have completed their circuits back to A. Add more objects only when the group is ready.

chapters.title: Learn the three-way cycle
chapters.text: Giants beat elves, elves beat wizards, and wizards beat giants. Practise tall, pointy-ear and spell-casting gestures with a clear gap between teams.

chapters.title: Choose one secret team character
chapters.text: Each team huddles and agrees on one character. Everyone in that team must reveal the same choice.

chapters.title: Reveal together across the gap
chapters.text: On the shared countdown, white performs giants and slate performs elves. Stay on your own side; this is the points version.

chapters.title: Award one point to the winner
chapters.text: Giants beat elves, so white earns one point. No chasing or capturing follows the reveal.

chapters.title: Matching characters produce a tie
chapters.text: In the next round, both teams choose wizards. Neither team scores; huddle and choose again.

chapters.title: Change who leads the huddle
chapters.text: Choose a new huddle leader for each round. Continue revealing one shared character per team until seven rounds are complete.

chapters.title: Compare points after seven rounds
chapters.text: This example ends with four white wins, two slate wins and one tie. White wins four–two. Equal totals would share the win.

chapters.title: Select the winker in secret
chapters.text: The detective looks away while a facilitator selects player 2. This teaching diagram reveals the secret; the detective must not be told.

chapters.title: The detective watches from the centre
chapters.text: The detective returns. Everyone looks around naturally without announcing who the winker is.

chapters.title: Wink at one player quietly
chapters.text: Player 2 makes eye contact and winks at player 5 while trying to avoid the detective’s attention. Only one player is targeted at a time.

chapters.title: The target makes a seated exit
chapters.text: Player 5 pauses briefly, then performs a seated dramatic exit and folds their arms. They are out of this short round.

chapters.title: A wrong guess uses one chance
chapters.text: The detective guesses player 4. That is wrong, leaving two guesses. Three wrong guesses would let the winker win.

chapters.title: A correct guess ends the round
chapters.text: The detective identifies player 2 on the second guess and wins. Also stop after two minutes; otherwise the winker wins.

chapters.title: Reveal, rotate, invite everyone back
chapters.text: Reveal the winker, change roles and bring every player back into the circle for another short round.

chapters.title: Leave one player without a spot
chapters.text: There is one fewer marked spot than people. One caller starts in the centre. Keep paths clear.

chapters.title: Call a fact true about yourself
chapters.text: The caller says, “The big wind blows for everyone who likes music!” In this example, players 1, 3 and 5 share that fact.

chapters.title: Walk to a non-adjacent open spot
chapters.text: Those players and the caller move. Choose a different spot more than one position away. Walk without grabbing or pushing.

chapters.title: The person left becomes caller
chapters.text: Player 5 has no spot, so becomes the new caller. Nobody is eliminated. If two people reach one spot together, pause and agree who stays.

chapters.title: No movement means another statement
chapters.text: Player 5 tries a true fact nobody else shares. Everyone stays put, so player 5 tries a new statement.

chapters.title: Keep discovering common ground
chapters.text: The new statement involves different people. Continue until several have called or five minutes pass, then share something the group discovered.
